summary:
[  edit  ]
The Lookup  TOP  replaces color values in the  TOP  image connected to its first input with values derived from a lookup table created from its second input or a lookup table created using the  CHOP  parameter. When using the 2nd input, the lookup table is created by defining a line (start and end position) on the  TOP  image. When using a  CHOP  the lookup table is created directly from the  CHOP 's values and the 2nd input is ignored.
The Index Range parameter can be used to define the minimum and maximum index values that will map to the first and last values in the lookup table. When the index goes outside of this range, it will  hold  on the first or last value of the lookup table. For example if the range is set to [0.1, 0.2], a value from the first texture of 0.15 will map to the middle of the lookup. A value of 0.1 (and below) will map to the dark end of the lookup and a value of 0.2 (and above) will map to the light end of the lookup.
See also  Remap TOP ,  Displace TOP .
Note:  This  TOP  supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.name: method
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose to use a line from the 2nd input (defined using UV coordinates) or  CHOP  values to define the lookup table.

parameters.label: 2nd Input, UV Coordinates
parameters.name: secondinput
parameters.description: Use the Dark UV and Light UV parameters to define the lookup table as a line extrated from the 2nd input.

parameters.label: CHOP  Values
parameters.name: chop
parameters.description: Use a  CHOP  referenced in th  CHOP  parameter to define the lookup table.

parameters.label: Index Range
parameters.name: index
parameters.description: ⊞  - The Index Range maps the index values to the lookup table's start and end and defaults to 0 and 1. The first parameter represents the start of the lookup table. When the index color has this value, it will index the start of the lookup table. The second parameter represents the end of the lookup table and behaves in the same way.  Note:  When the index goes outside of this range, it will  hold  on the first or last value of the lookup table.

parameters.label: index1
parameters.description: The minimum index value that maps to the start of the lookup table. Indices below this value will hold on the first value of the lookup table.

parameters.label: index2
parameters.description: The maximum index value that maps to the end of the lookup table. Indices above this value will hold on the last value of the lookup table.

parameters.label: Index  Channel
parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: ⊞  - The Index Channel controls how the color from the input is turned into a index to do the lookup. By default, the RGBA Independent option will do a separate lookup in each channel i.e. the red output channel will be based on the red value in the lookup table and the red value in the index image. For other options, like Luminance or RGBA Average, a single index value is calculated from the index color and all channels of the output image will be taken from the same pixel of the lookup table at the given index.

parameters.label: Independent Alpha
parameters.name: independentalpha
parameters.description: When enabled, the Alpha value of the output image is retrieved independently from the lookup table based on the alpha channel of the index image (the first input). This option can reproduce the legacy behavior of using the luminance to lookup the RGB values while using the alpha to separately lookup the alpha value. This option has no effect if using the 'RGBA Independent' or 'Alpha' index channel options since those modes already use the alpha channel as an index.

parameters.label: Dark UV
parameters.name: darkuv
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set the UV position to use for dark end of the lookup table. In the original image connected to the first input, any pixel with a value of (0,0,0) will be replaced by the value found at this UV position in the image connected to the second input.

parameters.label: Light UV
parameters.name: lightuv
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set the UV position to use for light end of the lookup table. In the original image connected to the first input, any pixel with a value of (1,1,1) will be replaced by the value found at this UV position in the image connected to the second input.

parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.name: chop
parameters.description: Reference  the  CHOP  to use to define the RGBA (A is optional) values in the lookup table.

parameters.label: Clamp  CHOP  Values
parameters.name: clampchopvalues
parameters.description: Clamps  CHOP  values between 0-1.

parameters.label: Output Lookup
parameters.name: displaylookup
parameters.description: Outputs the lookup table itself, instead of replacing the color values of the first input.

parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution.

parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.name: eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Half
parameters.name: half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 2X

parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 4X

parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Fits the width and height to the resolution given below, while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The width and height are limited to the resolution given below. If one of the dimensions exceeds the given resolution, the width and height will be reduced to fit inside the given limits while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Enables the  Resolution  parameter below, giving direct control over width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu

parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.name: fill

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best

parameters.name: outside

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. Making this larger than 1 is essentially the same as taking the output from each pass, and passing it into the first input of the node and repeating the process. Other inputs and parameters remain the same for each pass.

* **Normalize POP (POP de Normalización)** * **Función principal:** Re-escala los valores de posición XYZ (o cualquier otro atributo) a un **rango de 0 a 1**. * **Características clave:** * Puede convertir coordenadas cartesianas (XYZ) en **coordenadas polares o cilíndricas** (latitud, longitud, radio), también normalizadas a un rango de 0 a 1. * Ofrece opciones para **Bias** (sesgar los números hacia 0 o 1), aplicar una **función de curva de búsqueda** (`Lookup function`), un `Exponent` (potenciar valores) y **Re-range** (re-escalar a otro rango). * Permite asignar los valores normalizados a cualquier componente de un atributo float2, float3 o float4. * **Uso simple:** Útil para preparar datos para mapeo de texturas, shaders, o cualquier proceso que requiera valores dentro de un rango específico.
